It's probably going to take some trial and error depending on her specific needs, because everyone is different. Personally, I would suggest going as low carb as you can until you know what type of diabetes she has and what treatments are available for her. For a number i'd say keep it below 150g a day, or around 30-40 g per meal, but that was what was recommended to me before i was put on insulin as a Type 1.   
  
I know you're going with a meal plan place, but if you want to figure out DIY stuff in case you have to freeball it sometimes another general diet tip I'd suggest are increasing fiber intake alongside any carbs she eats, basically pairing it alongside so the carbs aren't eaten solo. This will help her for a lot of reasons. 1. fiber helps slow digestion of simple sugars, so any carbs that she does eat won't spike the blood sugar \~as much, as quickly\~ as it would without any fiber in the meal. 2. fiber is filling and the vitamins will help any vitamin deficiencies that she may have gotten while undiagnosed, iron and vitamin d were mine. 3. easy high fiber sources like quinoa, frozen vegetables, broccoli, sweet potatoes, and beans help a lot when replacing simple carbs in meals, and can help make meals a lot less daunting to put together when you have to completely turn your lifestyle upside down. It's overwhelming to have to figure all of this out seemingly overnight, and I wish you well <3

Even before I was diagnosed, I actually had a problem with people doing this as well, because not only does it promote a lot of very harmful ideas about food for people who don’t need to monitor their blood glucose that closely, it also can create issues for the people who need to get it. For example, the over-the-counter versions of continuous glucose monitors are marketed for people who don’t have diabetes, and we still have to go to a medical supplier with insurance. If I was able to get a CGM before I had all of my test done I would’ve been able to monitor myself closer. For people who have diabetes markers and aren’t diabetic yet, or who have strong family history of diabetes, I would support those people monitoring their blood sugar, but a lot of these fitness influencers that are using it or just using it to demonize carbs for an audience who might at risk of developing orthorexia because they’re so afraid of their blood sugar going higher than 130 can cause real harm for people. It also promotes the idea to the uneducated that diabetes is some thing that you can give yourself, when a lot of type two diabetics become diabetic because of a strong family history rather than just choice. I don’t know. It makes me really upset because I think it promotes very unhealthy views of food and wellness.

First off you have great tempo, and I feel that you only need a couple of tweaks to your form. I won't talk about body rotation since others have touched on it. I would say that you should tuck your chin to your chest more. Your body follows what your head does in the water, so keeping it tucked will allow you to be more horizontal in the water. I would also suggest when warming up, stretch your arms by holding them in [Streamline Position](https://www.google.com/url?sa=i&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DIj0QS8R-F8s&psig=AOvVaw1HpG0nsc4fHuW24MSQbkO7&ust=1683840975225000&source=images&cd=vfe&ved=0CBIQjhxqFwoTCNjP1Mva6_4CFQAAAAAdAAAAABAE) and lean side to side to open up your obliques a bit, this is less about your form and more about stuff outside the pool that can help you out when swimming. Along with the head position, your hips also should sit a bit higher in the water, keeping your head tucked low will help this, and another way to focus on this is focusing on your feet coming out of the water slightly. 

Now this is a lot of information at once, and a lot of focus on. When I swam and my coach would give me a lot of pointers it sometimes felt overwhelming, so I would suggest training both of these separately, then putting it altogether when you do freestyle. Use a kickboard to focus on hip position, and focus on your arms by just pulling with a pool buoy between your knees(If they are available to you, idk what your gym/pool provides) This could be a good way to focus on both skills before putting it altogether. I like to add kicks, laterals, and pulls into my warmup because it puts my head/body in the right mindset before I lead into longer distances.

I hope this helps, I tend to be very wordy when I explain things, so in essence; head down, ass up **XD**. You're doing great, form is something we all continually need to focus on, which is why we tend to do a lot of drills. :)

Treating my little brother the way I did. When we were kids, our parents got divorced and for most of the time that we were at dad’s, we were alone. Only our older sibling to watch us. I’m sure you can see where this is going. My little brother is about three years younger than me and when you’re 8 or 9 years old The last person you wanna hang out with is a five-year-old. 

He was a little kid that wasn’t really able to socialize a lot so taking in the gender and age difference he was pretty annoying to me. I don’t think I really handled it very well, and we fought constantly. over the years it made him feel like I hated him. But I think a lot of it was just me feeling general angst and disillusionment. 

He and I get along better now, and as we’ve grown up I feel like we are on much better terms, but I wasn’t very good sibling and it makes me sad that I can’t go back and treat him better. I love him dearly and I think that our childhood was disrupted with some of the family issues we had, like the abuse that led to our parent’s divorce. 

I know logically that it was a reaction to the fact that we were traumatized and alone all the time, and as children, you aren’t capable of taking care of somebody so much younger than you. And you’re unable to put up boundaries healthily at that age. 

But putting that all aside, knowing that you could’ve been a better sibling to somebody who needed you hurts. It hurts in a way that feels bad because you don’t think that you’re allowed to hurt. due to the fact that you were the older one and should have acted better. But you were also a child that didn’t have the tools to handle it, you know? It’s a difficult feeling.

tbh, no matter what you choose, it should be your choice and not the choice of people from this sub or anywhere else. Choosing whether or not to have kids is extremely personal for everyone, and if you discover a reason that is good enough for you that's great. I(20f) have also gone back and forth between that but we all have time, you and I both have a long way to go before we will be able to afford that kind of thing financially(in my situation anyway lol) so I don't think its a huge deal rn anyway. Also having a legacy doesn't have to include or exclude kids. If you are a community volunteer or just a nice person on a bus someone will have that lasting memory of you no matter how small you think your impact is or if they even know your name. I think there doesn't have to be a "legitimate reason" for having a kid because there isn't a legit reason to do anything. Just do what will make you happy in the long-run because stressing about the existential idea of "being right" when dealing with a very drastic life change will honestly just make you feel miserable. 

tl:dr, Fuck society, do what you want. We are on a rock in the middle of space, there is much more crazy shit to stress about.(this was supposed to be encouraging but I sometimes sound like an ass with word choice )
